summary: The TypeScript code compiles and Playwright APIs are used correctly. Asynchronous Playwright assertions correctly use await. Locator usage is proper with no direct iteration or array usage. However, selectors are weak because they rely on multiple hard-coded data-test attributes enumerated explicitly and may be brittle. The navigation assertion only checks for a generic URL fragment '/product/', which is not strong enough to confirm correct product detail page navigation. Also, test titles do not contain testCaseId values from generation mapping. No hard-coded waits or placeholder URLs are present.

issues.description: Selectors for product cards use multiple hard-coded data-test attributes in a single locator, which reduces maintainability and makes selectors brittle.
issues.recommendation: Use a more general attribute or class that identifies all product cards, or use a single data attribute that applies to all relevant elements.

issues.description: The navigation assertion checks only that the URL contains '/product/' after clicking a product card, which is too weak to confirm correct product detail page navigation.
issues.recommendation: Enhance the URL check by verifying the full path or parameters, or check page content specific to the product detail.

issues.description: Test titles do not include the corresponding testCaseId values (TC-001, TC-003) from the generation mapping.
issues.recommendation: Include testCaseId values in test titles for traceability between tests and requirements.

recommendations: Improve selectors by avoiding enumerated attribute lists.
Strengthen navigation URL assertions to verify correct detail page navigation.
Add testCaseId references to test titles for better traceability.
